title: Retro
lede: How a session retrospective finds what slowed the agent down, backed by evidence, and proposes fixes to its environment. Nothing changes until the user picks.

reconstruct.name: Reconstruct the session
reconstruct.role: On request, rebuild what happened from the conversation or a session log.
details: Runs only when the user asks for /retro; the current session is the default.
Cites concrete turns, commands, failures, corrections and repeated searches.
risks: If the record is unavailable, the retro reports the missing evidence and stops; it never infers struggles from the code alone.

trace.name: Trace causes
trace.role: Trace each struggle to a cause in the agent's environment.
details: Reads repo instructions, existing skills, check commands, hooks and CI wiring.
Asks whether a remedy already exists but was undiscovered, unwired or broken.
qs: Why look for a cause in the environment instead of blaming the agent's mistake?

classify.name: Classify and rank
classify.role: Sort findings into categories and rank them by impact and cost.
details: Prefers repairing an existing mechanism over adding a new one.
Keeps a remedy only if it would hold on a different task in the same repo; one remedy per finding.
A missing hook or CI check counts only when an error escaped or went undetected in this session, and a proposed check must be able to fire in the agent's normal workflow.
Ranks by impact and recurrence risk, weighed against cost and the upkeep of a new rule or check.

head: Category
Session signal
rows: Repeated searches or a hidden dependency delayed progress.
A mechanical error escaped, or a failure went undetected.
Relevant guidance was buried in instructions.
A call returned too much output or required repeated work.
Repetitive or ineffective steering used up context.
Missing logs, docs or read access blocked progress.

report.name: Report
report.role: A read-only table of findings with evidence and a recommended selection.

details.t: One row per finding (R-01, R-02 and so on)
more: Severity, session evidence, cause, proposed change and where it goes, cost, how to verify it, and when to remove it.

details: An empty result is valid after a smooth run.
risks: The retro edits nothing; installs, hooks, access changes and tasks wait for the user's choice.

route.name: Route selected work
route.role: The user picks remedies, and each goes to the skill that carries it out.

more: skillify for a reusable procedure, add-linter for linter setup, feature-chain for a substantial change.
upstream when the fix belongs in scaffold; improve, code-refiner or prune for code quality.

ci.d: Continuous Integration: checks that run on every push or PR.

hook.d: A script that runs automatically, for example before a commit.

steering.d: Written guidance that tells the agent how to behave.

ask.context: The reader wants to understand scaffold's /retro skill: how an AI agent reviews a session for friction and proposes environment fixes.
